summary: Teams analyze a real-world small business case and develop a strategic, data-driven growth plan. They present recommendations to address financial, operational, human resource, and marketing challenges, and respond to an additional scenario element at higher competition levels. The event includes both a prepared and an on-site component.
time_limits: No more than five (5) minutes orientation
No more than thirty (30) minutes preparation time for state and national levels
No more than three (3) minutes setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than ten (10) minutes judges’ questions
submission_requirements: One (1) copy of the Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual for each round of presentations (preliminaries and finals)
Signed BPA Release Form(s) for each round of presentations
AI Usage and Documentation Form for each round of presentations
deadlines: Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline
what_to_bring: Optional (Prep Room Only) – Laptop/notebook computer, portable printer with paper (1 per team)
Students may use one single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for their presentation
Optional - Prepared posters, graphs, poster board, flip charts and markers, product props (samples and promotional items)
competencies: Develop and implement a strategic action plan, effectively managing time, finances, and personnel to achieve measurable outcomes
Apply entrepreneurial, managerial, and problem-solving principles to address business challenges and develop innovative solutions
Interpret and communicate data-driven insights, identifying key issues, assumptions, and evidence to support business recommendations
Conduct financial and situational analyses using SWOT, forecasting, and other strategic tools to evaluate short- and long-term impacts
Analyze team strengths, define roles, and delegate responsibilities to meet project goals
Deliver a persuasive, data-supported team presentation using clear visuals and appropriate digital tools
Apply ethical, legal, and socially responsible decision-making in all business recommendations
Use digital collaboration and productivity tools to plan, analyze, and present business solutions
Evaluate business strategies using KPIs and analytics to measure performance and guide decisions
Use innovation and change-management principles to create and implement effective business solutions

judging_notes: Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestant within the time allotted
No internet access will be provided on-site at the NLC. Contestants may bring their own internet access, but it may be used only during their presentation—not in the prep room.
No materials may be left with the judges
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring.
If any required element question results in a NO, assign a score of 0 and stop scoring.
If there is no additional element, do not score the Inclusion of On-Site Information criterion.
PRESENTATION WILL BE STOPPED AT TEN (10) MINUTES
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged team event.
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants.
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked.
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified.
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
